verdicts.evidence: repro/A1-verify/rotation-race.mts against disposable PG18 (port 55701, migrated to head 0220), calling the real rotateRefresh / rotateRefreshToken / deactivateMember / updateMember / revokeUserOAuthTokens and the exact revoke SQL of routes/me.ts:186-203; output in repro/A1-verify/rotation-race.out.txt. A test-only AFTER INSERT trigger (pg_sleep 1s, scoped to the rotating connection) widens the real INSERT->COMMIT window. Results: self password change during an in-flight cookie rotation -> rotation ok, 1 live row left in the 'thief' family, successor rotates again (true); control without overlap -> rotate refused. Deactivation during rotation -> successor refused while inactive (auth.ts:217 returns ok:false WITHOUT revoking), then after updateMember({active:true}) the successor rotates (true), contradicting members.ts:220-221. OAuth: self password change during rotateRefreshToken -> 1 live row, successor rotates, carries the post-change credential_version (so bearer tokens are not stale); OAuth deactivate+reactivate before next presentation -> successor rotates (true).
verdicts.reason: Mechanism verified from code and reproduced: rotateRefresh/rotateRefreshToken lock only the token row (FOR UPDATE OF rt), never users; the revoke UPDATE in me.ts / revokeUserRefreshTokens / revokeUserOAuthTokens blocks on the old row, re-checks it after the rotator commits (now revoked, skipped) and never sees the successor inserted after its READ COMMITTED snapshot. Minted access tokens after the change pass stale (iat >= tokens_valid_after, cv current) and sessionLive. Severity stays P2 rather than P1: exploitation needs an already-stolen httpOnly refresh token plus winning a millisecond-scale INSERT->COMMIT window at the moment of the revoke (a tight refresh loop makes this a probabilistic, not deterministic, bypass); the unwidened timing was not measured. The OAuth deactivation variant is partly mitigated (presenting the successor while inactive revokes the family, tokens.ts:200), the cookie variant is not. Fix direction: lock the users row (SELECT ... FOR SHARE/KEY SHARE on users in rotate, or FOR UPDATE in the revokers) so rotation and revoke serialize, or have rotate re-check credential_version/tokens_valid_after against the token's issue time.
